preserved_failures: VirtualBox HPET has no FSB capability; mandatory watchdog admission failed before first user entry.
VirtualBox MADT assigns I/O APIC ID1 but live register remains reset0; reset-only initialization now requires an otherwise pristine controller.
Longer sessions exposed real zero-HPET-duration budget yields. Bounded actual timestamp resampling repairs them without fabricated charge.
Diagnostic harness initially dropped ENTRY because an exact firmware escape prelude shares its line; only that observed prefix is removed, with complete markers still validated.
Default diagnostic link reached210 pages and remained210 after constructor outlining. Shared log emitters recover capacity without raising208-page limit.
Default VirtualBox diagnostics reach stage117 peer-scheduler assertions; full diagnostic portability and VirtualBox-specific watchdog-delivery proof remain open.
Early host compile shadowed the device-page slice; iterator API initially broke the clock-driver two-page contract; restored pages() and separate device_pages().
Native compile caught unused routed proof; it is now consumed at quiescent dispatcher/proof boundaries.

First routed QEMU diagnostic recovered the watchdog but later failed stage4098: continuous-clock expected child mappings omitted the new I/O APIC leaf. The clock now retains the same complete child plan while mapping only its own APIC/HPET pair; exact equality remains enforced.
Watchdog proof originally hardcoded MSI. It now reports the actual transport and the routed qualifier requires hpet_ioapic; historical MSI summaries remain compatible.

Default VM helper was invoked after a failed build and failed before VM creation; its next run incorrectly encoded an already-bytes completion marker. Corrected separately, without passing the failed observations.
scope: Single BSP, one I/O APIC, unused masked non-legacy edge route; current QEMU optical and routed diagnostic regression plus two isolated VirtualBox serial application sessions. Not general shared IRQ/PCI routing, local GUI, packaged VirtualBox launch, production or full canonical qualification.
